chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Varsity Show: no script, a coal-shovel janitor bit
summary: With no music written they learned On With the Dance and Love Is on the Air; the director cast them as janitors, with Bubbles dancing while firing a furnace and Buck at the piano.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: No, just said movie. Just said movies, that's all. Got a contract for you for the movies. That's all. That's enough. And I figured he had a show, a picture for us so that did it. But he didn't have none because we lay off about two months almost before we got an answer back because I think it was either the last of January or the middle part of February before we got to California for the "Varsity Show" picture. And they didn't have no music or nothing written up and we rehearsed our act, we rehearsed a little bit here. They brought out the song, "On With The Dance" and "Love is on The Air," and we learned the (inaudible) songs and I found out I had to sing them, had to sing the songs but it

wasn't a part of our act now. It was a song that was supposed to go with the show but there wasn't nothing to match it. I was singing the song to Buck instead of singing the song to anybody in the show. And we did this show and I made up the part where you go in the basement to the furnace room where you shovel coal and I dance to shovel coal and Buck lays on the piano, instead of sitting up at the piano, he lays on the piano bench and plays with one hand while I'm dancing and firing the furnace to heat up the place. There's two janitors. Which was a sad thing. But the guy liked it anyway because it was entertaining.
He chose the role of janitors?

No. He don't choose anything to my estimation. It was the director that chose the part when he found out what we could do. He chose the costume and all as janitors and the property man fixed up the boiler room and the coal, which is gravel coal,
you know, like they use in furnaces, small grain. He fixed that all up for us and made it look like we were really working this thing.
How did you feel about playing a janitor?

All right, I didn't mind about that 'cause I was doing something to keep your mind off what I was, I had my mind on what I was doing, not what I was. See the difference there? So it come out all right.
